title: SLO-aware preemptive allocator for attention kernel queueing and jitter attenuation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: We observe intermittent latency spikes during mixed prefill+decode workload bursts when the kernel selector oscillates between FlashAttention variants. These spikes correlate with queueing thundering and sudden kernel handoffs, causing temporary SLO breaches for tail latency-sensitive customers. Goal: implement a SLO-aware preemptive allocator that performs admission control, preemptive kernel reservation, and jitter attenuation to reduce tail latency regressions while preserving throughput. The allocator should integrate with the existing kernel selection stack, prefer stable kernel bindings for warm contexts, and gracefully preempt resources when necessary without causing cascading evictions.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight preemptive allocator layer between request admission and kernel selection. Key behaviors: 1) Track per-GPU and per-tenant SLO budgets (tokens) and recent tail latency heatmaps. 2) On admission, classify request as latency-sensitive or throughput-tolerant via route metadata. 3) Reserve a small pre-warmed kernel slot for latency-sensitive prefill/decode requests; use adaptive thresholds to expand/contract reservation. 4) If GPU is saturated, preempt low-priority slots based on eviction score (age, coldness, remaining tokens) rather than LRU to avoid evicting critical KV cache entries. 5) Emit telemetry for every preemption decision and provide circuit-breaker fallback to a compatible fallback model variant (smaller/quantized) when repeated preemptions occur. Implementation will be pluggable with the existing kernel scorer and warmup manager and will expose a config knob in Console for reservation size and aggressiveness.
implementation_steps: Design data model: SLO token bucket and per-tenant heatmap window
Prototype allocator loop in runtime sandbox; add admission hook before kernel selection
Integrate eviction scoring with KV cache manager to avoid critical cache thrash
Add metrics/tags: preempt_count, preempt_reason, reservation_utilization, post-preempt-tail-latency
Run microbenchmarks with synthetic mix (prefill-heavy, bursty chat) on dev-hw
Create canary: 10% traffic on dedicated pool with telemetry-driven guardrails
Iterate on thresholds and fallback policies, document in Console runbook
test_plan: Unit tests for token bucket accounting and eviction scorer
Synthetic integration tests: ramp bursts with known shape and assert 99th latency improvement vs baseline
SLO regression test: run continuous 24h soak under mixed tenant workloads to validate no throughput regression >5%
Chaos test: force kernel selection failure and verify graceful preemption and fallback to compatible variant
A/B canary: compare canary pool vs control for tail latency and cost delta over 48h
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile latency reduced by >=20% for latency-sensitive route under reproduced burst profile
No more than 5% throughput regression for throughput-tolerant routes in canary
Preemptions have <1% false-positive rate (measured as preempt then immediately requeue within 50ms)
Telemetry exposed in Console with per-route breakdown and alerting on rapid preempt growth
notes: 2025-02-19: Spike repro harness created by Diego; initial runs show kernel handoff correlates with 99.9th tail latency
2025-02-25: Design review with Platform and Console; agreed to expose reservation size as Console knob and add guardrail alerts
2025-03-02: Prototype allocator reduces tail by ~28% in synthetic chat burst; memory thrash observed at extreme preemption aggressiveness
Next steps: tighten eviction scorer to consider per-request KV footprint and re-run 24h soak on staging
